# Purchase settlement
## Repeated delivery
An idempotency key identifies one purchase. Persist its receipt and return that receipt for repeated requests. Deduplication and the database commit share a transaction.

# Cancellation
## Operation lifetime
The caller owns an AbortSignal until every child has settled. A late response must not start persistence. Aborting a request does not undo an earlier commit.

# RPC budgets
## Histograms
Latency histograms retain tail observations. Report p50 and p95 rather than just the arithmetic mean. Separate server execution from queueing and transport time.

# Cache
Redis eviction starts when memory exceeds the configured maxmemory ceiling. Volatile policies require TTL metadata. Measure memory pressure before increasing capacity.

# Cache
A geocache is a hidden container discovered with coordinates. Log visits and replace its waterproof cover.

# Upstream capacity
An HTTP 429 response may carry Retry-After. Exponential backoff with jitter reduces synchronized retry storms. Do not automatically retry non-idempotent mutations.

# Congestion control
## Packet recovery
TCP retransmission recovers lost packets while a congestion window limits outstanding bytes. A receiver acknowledgement is evidence of delivery, not proof that the application committed a transaction. Timeout selection must account for measured round-trip variance. Repeated timeouts can reduce throughput even when the server has spare compute. Record packet loss and queue occupancy separately from service latency. A large socket buffer can hide a slow consumer temporarily, but increases retained memory and the time required to drain an overloaded connection. Backpressure should bound producer work before the transport queue grows without limit. Cancellation closes the local stream; it cannot establish whether a remote transaction committed. Application protocols therefore need stable request identities and explicit acknowledgement semantics. Keep retry policy with the operation that understands those semantics, and keep framing and partial-message handling with the transport.

# Presentation portability
PowerPoint substitutes missing fonts. Editable slide tables require text runs with explicit language and font metadata. A full-slide bitmap can conceal duplicate visible text.
